issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and timeliness
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction and that the appeal from the May 12, 2025 judgment was timely and properly perfected.

issues.label: Final appealable order
issues.why: The judgment entry must constitute a final appealable order covering conviction and sentence.

issues.label: Proper standard of review
issues.why: The court must select the correct standards (e.g., R.C. 2953.08(G)(2) for felony sentencing and Strickland for IAC) for each assignment.

issues.label: Record adequacy for review
issues.why: The court must ensure transcripts/entries (plea, sentencing, juvenile bindover materials if relevant) are sufficient to decide the claims.

issues.label: Mootness or waiver by guilty plea
issues.why: The court must determine whether the guilty plea waived any issues and whether the sentencing/IAC claims remain reviewable.

issues.label: Preservation and plain error
issues.why: The court must decide whether objections were required, whether error was preserved, and if not whether Crim.R. 52 plain-error analysis applies.

issues.label: Scope of sentencing appeal right
issues.why: The court must verify Arrington’s statutory right to appeal the sentence under R.C. 2953.08(A)(4) and any limits on review.

issues.label: Lawful adult-court jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm the general division had jurisdiction after transfer and indictment.

issues.label: Validity of juvenile transfer order
issues.why: If challenged directly or indirectly, the court must assess whether the bindover complied with R.C. 2152.10/2151.12 and due process.

issues.label: Probable cause waiver validity
issues.why: The court must consider whether Arrington’s waiver/stipulation at probable cause was knowing, intelligent, and voluntary if jurisdiction is disputed.

issues.label: Amenability hearing due process
issues.why: The court must ensure the amenability process satisfied statutory and constitutional requirements if it affects adult jurisdiction.

issues.label: Role of GAL and counsel in bindover
issues.why: The court must consider whether representation/GAL participation met juvenile-court protections relevant to transfer validity.

issues.label: Crim.R. 11 plea validity
issues.why: The court must confirm the guilty plea was knowing, intelligent, and voluntary under Crim.R. 11 and constitutional standards.

issues.label: Competency at plea/sentencing
issues.why: The court must consider whether there was any indicia Arrington was incompetent such that a competency inquiry was required.

issues.label: Factual basis for plea
issues.why: Although not always required, the court may consider whether the record supports the conviction under the indicted subsection.

issues.label: Correct offense degree and elements
issues.why: The court must verify the conviction matches R.C. 2903.11(A)(1) and the proper felony level for sentencing.

issues.label: Victim status corrections officer
issues.why: The court must determine whether any special victim status triggers enhancements or is merely factual background.

issues.label: Applicability of Reagan Tokes
issues.why: The court must decide whether an indefinite 7-to-10.5-year term is authorized for this F2 under current law.

issues.label: Indefinite term calculation
issues.why: The court must ensure the maximum term (10.5 years) correctly applies the statutory formula for the chosen minimum.

issues.label: F2 sentencing range compliance
issues.why: The court must verify the 7-year minimum is within the statutory range for a second-degree felony.

issues.label: Required sentencing findings
issues.why: The court must confirm whether any statutory findings were required (or not required) for the imposed term.

issues.label: R.C. 2929.11 and 2929.12 factors
issues.why: The court must confirm the trial court considered purposes/principles of sentencing and seriousness/recidivism factors.

issues.label: R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) applicability
issues.why: The court must determine whether Arrington qualifies as a 'child' for this provision because the offense occurred at age 17.

issues.label: Definition of 'child' at sentencing
issues.why: The court must interpret whether 'child' refers to age at offense, age at sentencing, or juvenile-court status for R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b).

issues.label: Mandatory youth-factor consideration
issues.why: The court must decide what the statute requires the judge to do to 'consider' youth and attendant characteristics.

issues.label: Adequacy of record showing consideration
issues.why: The court must determine whether the transcript/entry demonstrates the court actually considered youth factors as mandated.

issues.label: Need for explicit findings
issues.why: The court must decide whether R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) requires express findings on the record or allows implicit consideration.

issues.label: Youth factors scope and content
issues.why: The court must identify what constitutes 'youth and attendant characteristics' (immaturity, peer pressure, trauma, etc.) for this case.

issues.label: Consideration of psychological evaluation
issues.why: The court must decide whether the court was required to review or reference the February 2025 evaluation at sentencing.

issues.label: Sentencing hearing procedure compliance
issues.why: The court must assess compliance with R.C. 2929.19 hearing requirements (allocution, statements, victim input, PSI use).

issues.label: Allocution rights honored
issues.why: The court must ensure Arrington had the opportunity to speak before sentence was imposed.

issues.label: Right to counsel at sentencing
issues.why: The court must ensure Arrington was represented and counsel could present mitigation at sentencing.

issues.label: Presentence investigation requirements
issues.why: The court must determine whether a PSI was required, requested, waived, or necessary for lawful sentencing here.

issues.label: Juvenile history use at sentencing
issues.why: The court must evaluate how juvenile adjudications/history may be considered and whether any statutory limits apply.

issues.label: Constitutional proportionality concerns
issues.why: The court must consider Ohio Const. Art. I, § 9 proportionality arguments as framed by Arrington.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment youth jurisprudence relevance
issues.why: The court must determine whether Miller/Graham-type principles inform adult sentencing of juvenile offenders under Ohio law.

issues.label: Harmless vs prejudicial error
issues.why: If a youth-factor consideration error occurred, the court must decide whether it is reversible or harmless.

issues.label: Proper remedy for sentencing error
issues.why: The court must decide whether to vacate and remand for resentencing or provide other relief if R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b) was violated.

issues.label: Ineffective assistance framework
issues.why: The court must apply Strickland (deficient performance and prejudice) to counsel’s mitigation omissions.

issues.label: Deficient performance re youth mitigation
issues.why: The court must decide whether competent counsel would have presented youth-related mitigation given R.C. 2929.19(B)(1)(b).

issues.label: Prejudice from mitigation omission
issues.why: The court must decide whether there is a reasonable probability of a lesser sentence had youth factors been presented.

issues.label: IAC record-based review suitability
issues.why: The court must determine whether the ineffective-assistance claim is resolvable on direct appeal or requires postconviction evidence.

issues.label: Counsel’s strategic-choice assessment
issues.why: The court must consider whether the lack of mitigation presentation was a reasonable strategy or an unreasonable omission.

issues.label: Interaction of IAC and sentencing error
issues.why: The court must decide whether the alleged statutory error independently warrants remand, making IAC analysis redundant or altering prejudice.

issues.label: Invited error or waiver by defense
issues.why: The court must consider whether defense actions (e.g., agreeing to immediate sentencing) waived or invited the alleged errors.

issues.label: Effect of immediate sentencing after plea
issues.why: The court must consider whether proceeding immediately limited mitigation development and whether that affected statutory compliance.

issues.label: Notice of sentencing consequences
issues.why: The court must confirm Arrington was properly advised about indefinite sentencing consequences when pleading guilty.

issues.label: Postrelease control advisements
issues.why: The court must verify proper PRC notification (if applicable) at sentencing and in the judgment entry.

issues.label: Judgment entry sentencing completeness
issues.why: The court must ensure the entry contains all mandatory terms and advisements to be lawful and enforceable.

issues.label: Credit for time served
issues.why: The court must consider whether jail-time credit issues exist and whether they affect the sentence’s legality.

issues.label: Consecutive-sentence considerations
issues.why: The court must confirm no consecutive terms were imposed or, if they were, that required findings were made.

issues.label: Victim-impact and restitution issues
issues.why: The court must verify whether any restitution/costs were imposed and whether required procedures were followed.

issues.label: Court costs and indigency
issues.why: The court must consider whether costs were imposed lawfully and whether any indigency considerations were required.

issues.label: Adult prison placement legality
issues.why: The court must consider any statutory restrictions on housing youthful offenders in adult facilities pending and after sentencing.

issues.label: Equal protection or due process claims
issues.why: The court must address any implicit constitutional claims tied to sentencing a juvenile-transfer offender in adult court.

issues.label: Use of juvenile-court findings at sentencing
issues.why: The court must decide whether and how amenability findings (e.g., not amenable) may influence adult sentencing.

issues.label: Case law applicability (Patrick)
issues.why: The court must interpret and apply State v. Patrick and other precedent to the statutory youth-consideration requirement.

issues.label: Statutory interpretation of 2929.19(B)(1)(b)
issues.why: The court must construe the statute’s text, purpose, and effective-date/application to Arrington’s sentencing.

issues.label: Retroactivity/effective-date issues
issues.why: The court must confirm the youth-factor statute was in effect for the sentencing date and applies to this case posture.

issues.label: Appropriate disposition on each assignment
issues.why: The court must separately resolve each assignment of error and specify the resulting judgment (affirm, reverse, remand).
